To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the goldfish radial glia transcriptome was assembled and that secretoneurin-A modulates neurogenic and inflammatory networks.
we identified a diverse repertoire of hormones, peptides and cytokines that may be involved in the neuroglial interactions of teleost radial glia.
the first transcriptome for teleost RGCs was generated and that SNA modulates neurogenesis and inflammation-related transcriptional networks in fish RGCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and functional characterization of novel neurogenic and inflammatory pathways in teleost RGCs, which will provide a foundation for further studies investigating the role of RGCs in the regulation of neurogenesis and neuroendocrine-immune interactions in teleost fish.
the identification of novel genes and pathways in goldfish RGC transcriptomes that may provide insights into the role that RGCs play in neurogenesis, neurosteroidogenesis, and neuroinflammation.
the role of RGCs in the brain of goldfish.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present study is the first to identify a comprehensive gene expression profile in goldfish RGC and the first study that identifies the molecular mechanisms by which SNa regulates neurogenic and immune functions in goldfish brain.
the RGC transcriptome is a rich source of information on RGC function and that SNa is a potent regulator of RGC gene expression.
this is the first study to characterize the transcriptome of goldfish RGC and to identify the SNa-regulated transcriptome in RGCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a transcriptome for goldfish radial glia and identify SNa as a regulator of neurogenic and inflammatory networks.
the SNa transcriptome of goldfish RGC is enriched for genes involved in neurogenesis and inflammatory signaling, and SNa is predicted to be a potent modulator of RGC physiology.
the RGC transcriptome and its response to SNa provides novel information about the molecular and cellular functions of this important cell in the fish brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SNa is an essential regulator of neurogenic and inflammatory processes in RGCs and may play a role in the modulation of neuronal-glial interactions.
RGCs have an extensive and complex transcriptome that is responsive to SNa and that these cells are likely involved in a diverse array of physiological processes.
SNa is a novel and potent mediator in teleost RGCs.
